theo: The joy of Christmas is followed by the tears of Bethlehem. Herod, furious at being tricked by the Magi, kills all the boys of Bethlehem two years old and under. Matthew hears in the mothers' cry the voice of Rachel weeping in Ramah. From Abel onward, innocent blood has cried out to God; the Holy Innocents are the first to die in place of Christ.

The Church honours them as martyrs who witnessed to Christ not by speaking but by dying. On this day Kerala's Church celebrates Holy Childhood Day: children praying and sharing for other children. We also remember all innocent children who suffer today: the unborn, abused, trafficked, hungry and war-torn. Jeremiah's promise stands: “there is hope for your future.”

illus: A couple in Kannur who lost their baby daughter a few days after birth began a small fund in her name to help poor mothers deliver safely in hospital. They said: “Our tears became a river for other children.”

homily: Dear friends, the joy of Christmas is followed by tears. Herod, furious at being tricked by the Magi, killed all the children in and around Bethlehem who were two years old or under (Matthew 2:16). Matthew hears in the mothers' cry the voice of Rachel weeping for her children; she refused to be consoled, because they are no more (Matthew 2:18; Jeremiah 31:15).

The first reading takes us back to the beginning: Cain kills his brother Abel (Genesis 4:8). From the first family, innocent blood has cried to God. The Holy Innocents join this long line, and they are the first to die in the place of Christ.

Why does God allow this? We do not have a full answer. But Christmas tells us that God did not stay distant from suffering. He came into a world where children are killed, and he himself would be killed. He is with the innocent who suffer.

The Letter to the Hebrews speaks of those who suffered for their faith: they were stoned, sawn in two, killed by the sword; of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:37–38). The Holy Innocents could not speak, but their lives witnessed to Christ.

Today the Church in Kerala keeps Holy Childhood Day: children praying for and sharing with other children. Let us remember the innocents of today: unborn children lost to abortion, children who are abused, trafficked, starving or caught in war. Herod is still at work.

Jeremiah gives a promise: there is hope for your future, says the Lord (Jeremiah 31:17). Let us protect children in our families and parishes, defend the unborn, and support children in need. And let us comfort parents who grieve the loss of a child. Amen.
kids: Children, today is your special day! Pray for children who are sad, hungry or in danger, and share something to help them.

intro: The Holy Innocents and Holy Childhood Day.

sub: Abel's blood cries from the ground.
God is never deaf to the innocent.
q: And the LORD said, “What have you done? Listen; your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground!”
When Herod saw that he had been tricked by the wise men, he was infuriated, and he sent and killed all the children in and around Bethlehem who were two years old or under.
points.apply: Pray for children who suffer violence.

sub: Jeremiah's lament becomes the cry of Bethlehem.
God promises a future of hope.
q: Thus says the LORD: Keep your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears; for there is a reward for your work, says the LORD.
A voice was heard in Ramah, wailing and loud lamentation, Rachel weeping for her children; she refused to be consoled, because they are no more.
points.apply: Console a mother who has lost a child.

sub: The Innocents' treasure is with God.
Children who share store up treasure in heaven.
q: But the righteous live forever, and their reward is with the Lord; the Most High takes care of them.
But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consumes and where thieves do not break in and steal. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
points.apply: Help children share a gift with poor children.

concl: Let us protect and serve the little ones.
